purpose: Design-only rollback contract for a real P5B cutover. Not executed in this session -- no cutover occurred, so no rollback was needed or performed. Documents the procedure that would be used, built on the orders proven safe in this R1's live testing.

rollback_sequence.detail: Use the exact order proven safe in this R1: stop watchtower_api, then creator_funding_worker, then watchtower_listener. Measured real durations from this session: ~10.25s + ~15.20s + ~0.12s = ~26s total.

Run the exact 6-signal check qualified in this R1 (supervisor state, process census, lsof handles, write-lock state, WAL stability, MAX(id) polling) before proceeding. Must reach PASS before any rollback file operation.

Revert whatever switch mechanism was used (e.g. re-point the symlink/config back to the original database/flex_complete_database.db path, or restore the pre-switch DB_PATH env var in supervisord.conf if that was the switch mechanism). This step's exact mechanics depend on what the real P5B switch implementation turns out to be -- not designed or executed in this R1, which is writer-quiesce-mechanics-only in scope.

Confirm the restored target is genuinely the original DB and not a partially-migrated or corrupted intermediate state -- e.g. compare a fingerprint (file size, row counts on key tables, MAX(id) on transfer_index matching the last known-good pre-switch value) against a pre-switch baseline captured in step 1's zero-writer-proof snapshot.

Use the exact order proven safe in this R1: start watchtower_listener, then creator_funding_worker, then watchtower_api. Measured real durations from this session: ~11.16s + ~5.25s + ~8.67s = ~25s total.

Confirm all three RUNNING and stable for at least 15-20s (no crash loop, matching this R1's stability-window methodology), API health check returns 200/302, auto_extract_funders toggle value unchanged from pre-rollback, and MAX(id) on transfer_index eventually advances again under organic traffic (or listener log shows live WS event processing as a faster proxy signal, per this R1's Part 10 methodology).

restart_target_contract_dependency: This rollback sequence depends on the restart-target-contract finding (storage_lifecycle_p5b_r1_restart_target_contract.json): since all three services resolve DB_PATH as a module-level constant at import time, a full stop/start (step 1 and step 5 above) is REQUIRED and SUFFICIENT to make each service pick up the restored old-DB target after step 3/4 -- no service needs any additional signal, reload, or special handling to complete the rollback.
risk_assessment: Low risk by design: the three writer services are DB CLIENTS, not the DB itself. A stop/start cycle of these services carries no data-loss risk on its own (proven in this R1: creator_funding_worker's DB-backed checkpoint resumes correctly, no queue rows lost or duplicated across a real stop/start cycle). The only genuine risk in an aborted real cutover lies in the DB-file-level operations themselves (delta copy, identity reconciliation, atomic switch) -- those remain out of scope for this R1's rollback contract and would need their own P5A-referenced rollback design (see docs/audits/storage_lifecycle_p5a_part*.json for whatever was already benchmarked there).
verdict: ROLLBACK_CONTRACT_CONSTRUCTIBLE -- a safe rollback target proof exists, built directly on this R1's own measured, live-verified stop/start orders and the restart-target contract; the file-level portion (steps 3-4) is deferred to whatever the real switch implementation turns out to be, consistent with this milestone's scope boundary (writer-quiesce mechanics only, no actual cutover).
